meta.title: Installation
meta.description: Install React Scheduler, add its stylesheet, and render the first schedule. Peer dependencies, the styles, and a five-line check.

peers.intro: React Scheduler installs nothing of its own. Its two peers are the React you already have; every other package in the tree is a development tool of this repository, not of your application.
rows: Hooks, context and the concurrent renderer the views are built on.
The DOM renderer, and the portal the overflow and detail dialogs open in.

stylesheet.intro: Import the stylesheet once, where your application starts. It carries both presets, the light and the dark scheme, and the three densities; nothing is injected at runtime.
stylesheet.unstyled: If you want to style everything yourself, import @react-schedulerkit/react-scheduler/base.css instead: the same structure with no colors, no spacing scale and no type scale. See Customization for the levels in between.

verify.intro: This is a complete file. If it renders a card in one shift, the package, its styles and its peers are in place.
verify.height: Scheduler fills its container and scrolls inside it, so give the container a height — a fixed one, or a flex or grid cell that has one. Without it, the schedule grows with its content and the shift buttons have nothing to scroll.
verify.callout: Both are optional. Without date the schedule shows the current day, and without shifts it uses two twelve-hour shifts anchored at 08:00.
